content.comment_body: Hello everyone, I'm facing an issue in my application and looking for advice. The process involves repeatedly cooling and heating a liquid to setpoints that can be configured via the display. While I have the core sequence working, I've hit a snag when adding a bar graph to show the liquid's temperature changes. Although min and max values can be manually set for the bar graph, I want them to be dynamically linked to the cooling and heating setpoints, updating whenever those change on the display. Is it possible to achieve this? I've been trying different approaches, but haven't found a solution. Any suggestions are welcome! For reference, I'm working with [product_name] and [product_name] [version_no].
Unfortunately, this isn't possible because the MinValue and MaxValue parameters can't be changed during runtime.
That's disappointing, it would have made the visualization much more dynamic! Thanks for clarifying.
Sorry, but there really isn't an alternative solution for this limitation.

If you’re looking for a workaround, there's an example attached where the bar graph operates within adjustable parameters. Sometimes approaching the problem differently helps. Since the bar graph scaling is fixed when programming, consider using a fixed range (for example, 0 to 1000) and adjust your value to fit this scale for visualization purposes. Regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: Users are trying to set dynamic min/max ranges for bar graph displays on [product_name] hardware, based on changing setpoints. However, current software limitations mean these values cannot be updated in real time, which restricts interactive monitoring capabilities. Alternatives discussed include normalizing values to a fixed scale instead of implementing fully dynamic visualization.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect to be able to adjust the bar graph's min and max in real time as setpoints change, allowing for more accurate and flexible visualization during operation.
